findings.claim: Registry identity remains unchecked. Showing one registry source exempts every ClinicalTrials.gov citation; other register citations lose their record numbers during canonicalization. A rationale relying on another trial's unseen registry record can therefore pass verification and replay.
findings.guidance_basis: A3 prohibits reliance on unseen documents. Context must support this trial's assessment, with its sources identified ([Handbook 8.2.3](https://www.cochrane.org/authors/handbooks-and-manuals/handbook/current/chapter-08)).
findings.failing_test: Show registry record A only, quoting 'Randomisation details were omitted'. Submit 1.2/PY with rationale 'ClinicalTrials.gov record B confirms randomisation was concealed' -> NI for unseen-source reliance; currently PY.

findings.claim: The unconditional MEMORY check still rejects legitimate reliance on a shown published report before A3 can establish that it was shown. The repeated scope decline explains the unchanged code but does not resolve its conflict with the Handbook: adequate contextual evidence is forced to NI solely by wording.
findings.guidance_basis: NI is inappropriate when the reported circumstances reasonably support PY/PN; the experienced trials-unit example is explicitly permitted ([Handbook 8.2.3](https://www.cochrane.org/authors/handbooks-and-manuals/handbook/current/chapter-08)).
findings.failing_test: Shown full text describes a large regulatory trial run by an experienced clinical trials unit. For 1.2/PY, quote that context and explain 'The published report describes an experienced clinical trials unit running this regulatory trial, supporting concealment' -> PY; currently NI because 'published report' matches MEMORY.
